comment: What the black sweep leaves alone. py/main_repo_util.py --run-black reads this file through py/repo_util/maintenance_policy.py and applies it to every swept repo except MAM-basics, which formats its own originals: a vendored copy is maintained in its source repo, so reformatting the copy would only make the next sync noisier. global.source_pkg_dirs: each key is a package name that black skips as a directory at any depth, and only the keys are read. overrides: single files copied out of MAM-basics to paths of their own; there are none. foreign_vendored: files copied into a swept repo from a source repo other than MAM-basics. Its one entry is MAM-private's frozen pointed-ketiv archive, whose README says its algorithm modules are copied byte for byte from an earlier MAM-private commit and whose source-manifest.json pins each module's SHA-256; Black would rewrite nine of the ten, which the 2026-10-07 maintenance sweep did before the change was reverted. Among the directories the package names cover are MAM-private's copies mgketer/py/mb_cmn and mgketer/py/mb_diff_mpu, made by MAM-private/mgketer/py/main_update_vendored_files.py, and al-hatorah/py/mb_cmn, made by MAM-private/al-hatorah/py/main_update_vendored_files.py, each script copying by intersection with this repo's package of the same name. Nothing measures whether those copies have drifted. record_dirs: folders of records in a swept repo, each named with a trailing slash, which black skips as whole subtrees. Its one entry names three MAM-private folders of records whose bytes are pinned by SHA-256 manifests or are dated provenance; the 2026-11-11 dry run found that Black would rewrite 47 of their files, and Ben chose on 2026-11-11 to exclude them by folder.
